glosses: flow
flow (style)
Flux, rythme avec lequel le rappeur débite les paroles.
État de motivation et d'attention focalisées qui permet de mobiliser au mieux ses facultés et d'atteindre une performance optimale.

examples.text: Une attention quasi maniaque est nécessaire, et la négligence est interdite. Selon lui, l’accès à ce niveau de concentration requiert même un état de l’esprit tout à fait particulier qu’on appelle le “flow” (en français dire le “flux” ou alors “la zone”, mais la notion est mieux identifiée en psychologie positive dans son expression anglaise, bien qu’on la doive à un professeur de psychologie hongrois du nom de Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi).

glosses: Style.

examples.text:
J’ai cramé ton flow, je vois de quel genre t’es
J’sais qu’on va s’entendre j’ai de la monnaie

glosses: Movement in people or things characterized with a continuous motion, involving either a non solid mass or a multitude.
The movement of a real or figurative fluid.

examples.text: Mr. Cooke at once began a tirade against the residents of Asquith for permitting a sandy and generally disgraceful condition of the roads. So roundly did he vituperate the inn management in particular, and with such a loud flow of words, that I trembled lest he should be heard on the veranda.

glosses: A formalization of the idea of the motion of particles in a fluid, as a group action of the real numbers on a set.

examples.text: The notion of flow is basic to the study of ordinary differential equations.

glosses: The rising movement of the tide.
Smoothness or continuity.

examples.text: The room was small, but it had good symmetry and flow.

glosses: The amount of a fluid that moves or the rate of fluid movement.

examples.text: Turn on the valve and make sure you have sufficient flow.
Other devices measure water flow in streams fed by melted ice.

glosses: A flow pipe, carrying liquid away from a boiler or other central plant (compare with return pipe which returns fluid to central plant).
A mental state characterized by concentration, focus and enjoyment of a given task.

examples.text: The point about flow is that it is enjoyable. As research has shown "the more often athletes experienced flow, the happier they were." But the second is that entering flow actually improves performance.

glosses: The emission of blood during menstruation.

examples.text: Tampons can be small or large, slender or thick. From “slender” to “super”, you can pick the size that matches your flow.

glosses: The ability to skilfully rap along to a beat.

examples.text: The production on his new mixtape is mediocre but his flow is on point.
Now shawty said she feelin' my style, she feelin' my flow […] / My flow, my show brought me the dough / That bought me all my fancy things

glosses: The sequence of steps taken in a piece of software to perform some action.

examples.text: login flow
search flow
I'm setting up event tracking for a pretty standard, multi-step signup flow, and I'm wondering [...]

glosses: To move as a fluid from one position to another.

examples.text: Rivers flow from springs and lakes.
Tears flow from the eyes.
Wrex: I need to get my blood flowing. Find me something to kill!

glosses: To proceed; to issue forth; to emanate.

examples.text: Wealth flows from industry and economy.
Those thousand decencies that daily flow / From all her words and actions.

glosses: To move or match smoothly, gracefully, or continuously.

examples.text: The writing is grammatically correct, but it just doesn't flow.
Virgil […] is […]sweet and flowing in his hexameters.

glosses: To have or be in abundance; to abound, so as to run or flow over.

examples.text: […] in that day[…] the hils shall flow with milke[…]
the exhilaration of a night that needed not the influence of the flowing bowl

glosses: To hang loosely and wave.

examples.text: a flowing mantle
flowing locks
[…]the imperial purple flowing in his train.

glosses: To rise, as the tide; opposed to ebb.

examples.text: The tide flows twice in twenty-four hours.
The river hath thrice flowed, no ebb between.

glosses: To arrange (text in a wordprocessor, etc.) so that it wraps neatly into a designated space; to reflow.
To allow (a liquid) to flow.

examples.text: The action is usually progressive, and as a certain amount of oil is flowed from the tubing it lowers the pressure on the remaining oil and liberates more gas, thus causing additional oil to flow from the tubing.

glosses: To cover with water or other liquid; to overflow; to inundate; to flood.
To cover with varnish.
To discharge excessive blood from the uterus.
A bog or mire, especially a rough, waterlogged one.

examples.text: […] there are other extensive mosses in this district, commonly called flowes, which it is not probable ever will, or ever can be, converted into arable land. Some of these flowes are found to be 20, 25, or 30 feet deep, and are, besides, such a dead level, that the water has little or no descent; and even supposing they should be cast, or burnt to the bottom, standing pools of dirty water could only stand in their place.
Ye'll stick in some flow, Or, ye'll melt in a thow
Had been roughly laid with bog-wood dug from the flowes,
Dandering o'er ferney knowes, [...] Springing o'er bogs an' flowes, [...]
If dey wirna a day apo' da flow dan he [it] wis nae man's bishaness.
